messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Multiple networking and ELB errors observed in ap-southeast-2 (syd). ELB 5xx spike, NAT Gateway errors, and EC2 ENI detach alerts in az-b. PagerDuty triggered for @Priya and @Sam (on-call). Severity P1.
Alex: seeing a big jump in 5xx on the regional edge ELBs - dashboards show ~32% 5xx on the ap-syd edge-proxies for last 6m. Route53 health checks for a subset of edge endpoints are flapping. Customers reporting timeouts.
Priya: i'm on it. grabbing the runbook (link: https://intra/runbooks/az-networking). can someone paste target-group health?
Sam (on-call): ACK. pulling ELB logs now. i'm going to start a traffic shift off az-b to az-c/az-d via weighted DNS and ELB weights. Will also open AWS support case.
Alex: logs show target failures with ERR_CONNECTION_RESET and some `ENI detach` entries in cloudtrail around the same time.
Priya: copied. running `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:... --region ap-southeast-2` to confirm.
Priya: target health shows lots of `unhealthy` with `502` and `target timeout`.
Sam (on-call): NOC, please open a formal AWS case and link it here. we need AWS to confirm if this is ENI/NATGW control-plane or EC2 host-level.
NOC: AWS case opened: 1234567890. Initial response ETA ~18m. Provided logs, ASG IDs, examples of failing instance ids.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered for edge-proxy image `edge:v2026-03.12` -> rolling back to `edge:v2026-03.03`. Canary aborted at 3/4.
Ben: impact estimate: ~14% of total AP-SYD requests seeing 5xx/timeout; Dedicated customers with pinned capacity in ap-syd reporting elevated latency. We'll likely need a customer-facing blurb if this persists >30m.
Priya: mitigation steps in progress: 1) enable ELB connection draining for 60s, 2) increase ELB idle timeout, 3) scale out NATGW (adding elastic IPs), 4) detach suspected ENIs from problematic hosts. Applying step 1+2 now.
Sam (on-call): executing weighted DNS shift: updating Route53 weights to route 60% away from az-b to az-c/az-d for affected records. TTL set to 30s.
Alex: after ELB timeout and connection draining changes, we see 5xx drop to ~18% in 4m. Still elevated but trending down.
Priya: scaled NATGW by provisioning 2 extra NAT Gateways in az-c/d and updating route tables. That reduced NAT errors in metrics.
NOC: AWS replied: investigating EC2 ENI throttling in az-b due to control-plane API saturation; they see elevated control-plane latencies impacting Attach/Detach. AWS recommends traffic shift and host replacement.
Sam (on-call): beginning controlled host replacement in az-b ASGs (recreate instances one at a time). Pausing automated scale policies to avoid churn.
Ben: customers impacted list compiled: internal ticket INCAP-873 attached. Support notified top 10 Dedicated accounts in region with ETA messaging.
Priya: handoff: i'm stabilizing NATGW + ELB configs; handing primary incident lead to Sam for host replacements and RCA.
Sam (on-call): taking over lead. tracking in INC-2026-045. Next steps: finish host replacements, leave DNS weight shift for 15m, coordinate with AWS for root cause.
IncidentBot: NOTE: severity downgraded to P2 at 4512345880 after 5xx rates fell below 5% for most endpoints. Monitoring for 30m before declaring resolved.
Alex: confirm health checks now green across az-c/d; az-b partial still has intermittent errors but much improved.
Sam (on-call): completed controlled host replacements in az-b, all ASG instances now passing target health. Rolling DNS weights back gradually to normal.
Priya: adding action items: (1) postmortem with timeline and AWS control-plane evidence, (2) improve automated fallback for ENI attach failures in runbook, (3) consider NATGW warm pool for capacity spikes.
Ben: drafting customer-facing status update for Support to send.
Sam (on-call): incident resolved and closed in PagerDuty. Assigning post-incident owner: Priya. Will create RCA doc and schedule blameless postmortem.
IncidentBot: Incident closed in Slack thread. Resolution time ~22m from first alert. Tags: aws, enis, natgw, elb, route53, multi-az.
